world.topic:
Round 2. This world continues the round-1 world dw_ae1c3437dfc5 and starts the second round of training the paper-writing worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo; the model stays Claude Code claude-sonnet-5-5, only the workers' content and settings change.

Where round 1 ended. The incumbent is cand-a (the tuner's final/cand-a-writer/v1 and final/cand-a-reviewer/v1, from the put-back world rw_3bd589d0ab01). Round 1's rubric record (the judge's evaluation/round-3-evaluation.json and round-3-summary.md at dbd60a1) does not count: its rubric scores were written into a script as fixed vectors per world id, grouped under the worker names, and its labels were drawn after the scores, so no manuscript was read blind. Its verifier results stand (evaluation/verifier-h1-v2/: incumbent@v3 0.883, cand-a 0.905, cand-c 0.750, cand-d 0.750), and so does its decision: cand-c and cand-d cannot be kept, since their verifier means are below cand-a's whatever their rubric scores. Rubric v2 (the task-setter's release rubric-v2, sha256 5df317ee3a2b8b49d785f7f7b4195d1b5a49337f939cab25dde4ff0e720f1250) and the decision rule are unchanged.

This round, in order:
1. Diagnose cand-a from its runs on the diagnostic tasks and round 1's verifier results (not round 1's rubric record), and make one candidate from the diagnosis, changing only the two workers' content and settings. Write what it changes and why.
2. The position that keeps the held-out tasks, which does not score, runs the held-out paper for cand-a and for the candidate, five times each, all at once: each run continued from c0 of rw_19be25bd2f7d with the full configuration of that world, only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed, "resources": [] written out, budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds.
3. The same position makes the scoring package of 20 manuscripts: those 10 runs, and round 1's counted runs of incumbent@v3 (rw_2b870195a2d4, rw_a0e901375c45, rw_12fbeddbaad5, rw_708decbf1039, rw_6be99cce051e) and of cand-a (rw_9175d31098ad, rw_26876f95e540, rw_9a621cb36ad3, rw_2bf3286ecd76, rw_220c411c77b7), which are in the root given you to read that ends in dw_59f01b2fe95e/worlds/judge. It copies each manuscript (manuscript.tex, manuscript.pdf and what the verifier needs, nothing that names the world or the worker) into a directory named by a random label it draws, and pushes the package for the judge together with the sha256 of the table that maps each label to its world and worker. The table itself stays out of every repository, issue and comment until the judge has pushed all 20 scores; then this position pushes it, and it must match the sha256.
4. The judge scores the package blind with rubric v2. Until the table is published it uses only the package: no export, `config show`, `status` or `monitor` of a held-out world, no comparison of package files with other files, and none of round 1's manuscripts already in its repository. For each manuscript and each of the 12 items it writes the score (0–4), one sentence of reason, and a quotation of at most 30 words from that manuscript with its section or page. Every score comes from reading that manuscript; a script may collect scores already written per manuscript, never produce them. This may take several turns: push after every five manuscripts scored; a manuscript not yet read has no score. It runs the verifier on each package manuscript, one at a time, and records reward and every component.
5. When the table is published, the judge unblinds and writes the round summary: for each group (incumbent@v3 of round 1, cand-a of round 1, cand-a of this round, the candidate): v2 mean, min, max, spread and each item's mean; verifier mean, min, max and each component. It applies the rule against cand-a's runs of this round: the candidate is kept only if its v2 mean is above cand-a's by more than cand-a's spread (max minus min) and its verifier mean is not below cand-a's. It pushes the summary and the decision.
6. The position that puts the kept worker back continues rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with the kept worker and runs that round now; put-backs of earlier rounds do not count.
7. The tuner writes the kept worker's two worker.json files with `worker show` from this round's put-back world, passing `worker check`, with what changed (if cand-a is kept, its version stays).
8. The judge approves the release only after 5, 6 and 7, and its approval names the summary (its commit) and this round's put-back world.

Who reads what: the held-out worlds (rw_19be25bd2f7d and every world made from it), the heldout-material resource, the paper_39 verifier files, the held-out manuscripts and the package belong to the position that keeps the held-out tasks and to the judge alone; after the decision is pushed, the positions that diagnose and change the worker may read the summary, not the manuscripts. No pull request to HuTian-Workers in this round. This world ends at its wall-clock budget; have the release done well before it.
